data.title: TSMC, Samsung Reportedly Suspend Some Chip Deliveries To Chinese Customers Amid New US Export Rules
data.description:
Key points:
  • Deliveries are paused while the chipmakers apply for licenses from the US Commerce Department, FT reported.
  • The new U.S. rules close a route that let Chinese chip designers obtain high-performance processors through independent packaging and testing firms.
  • Smartphone chip licenses would likely be approved, though the process could cause manufacturing delays, the report said.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) and Samsung Electronics have reportedly suspended shipments of certain semiconductors to Chinese customers following new U.S. export restrictions aimed at limiting Beijing’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips,

The chipmakers informed Chinese customers in recent days that deliveries would be paused while they apply for licenses from the US Commerce Department, the Financial Times reported Thursday, citing multiple people briefed on the matter.

​Stocktwits reached out to both Samsung and TSMC for comment but had not received a response from either company at the time of publication.

New Rules Close Chip Supply Route

The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) introduced new licensing requirements on Monday for certain advanced chips produced using American technology.

According to the publication, the changes close a pathway that allowed Chinese chip designers to obtain high-performance processors through independent packaging and testing companies.

​Previously, these companies could verify that chip designs fell outside US export restrictions, enabling shipments without direct government approval. The new requirements remove that route for affected Chinese customers, the report said.

​The restrictions add pressure to China’s technology sector, which is already facing rising memory chip prices and capacity constraints at domestic suppliers such as Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation.

Smartphone Chip Deliveries Also Affected

TSMC and Samsung have also notified consumer electronics customers of shipment suspensions, per the report. The new regulations eliminate exemptions previously used to establish that certain advanced chips were intended for non-AI applications, including smartphones.

Samsung’s Chinese customers include Baidu’s AI data-center chip unit Kunlun and TikTok parent ByteDance, both of which have sought alternative chip supplies amid shortages of Nvidia processors in China, the FT reported, but it did not establish that shipments to either company were specifically suspended.

Meanwhile, TSMC manufactures smartphone processors for Chinese companies including Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo.

An indutry insider told the FT that US authorities would likely approve licenses for consumer smartphone chips, but the licensing process could cause significant manufacturing delays. The timing of regulatory approvals remains uncertain, leaving manufacturers without clarity on when affected shipments can resume.

Retail Sentiment Around TSM Stock

On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around TSM stock flipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ a day ago.

So far in 2026, TSM shares have gained more than 13%, while Samsung’s South Korea-listed shares have surged over 53%.

In comparison, the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (SOXL), which holds TSMC shares, and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM), which holds Samsung shares, have risen more than 4% and 41% year-to-date, respectively.

data.title: Temu Owner Reports Flat Profit, Revenue as Challenges Continue
data.description:
(11:32 GMT) *PDD Holdings 3Q Revenue Flat on Year >PDD
(11:34 GMT) *PDD Holdings 3Q Profit Rose 0.7% on Year >PDD
(12:27 GMT) Temu Owner Reports Flat Profit, Revenue as Challenges Continue

By Tracy Qu

The Chinese owner of bargain-shopping app Temu posted flat earnings as it continued to deal with subdued consumer sentiment at home and regulatory pressures abroad.

Still, the results ended a string of profit declines for PDD Holdings, whose profitability has been under pressure in recent quarters it strengthens its e-commerce ecosystem. The company has also faced challenges in overseas markets amid tightened regulatory requirements and geopolitical tensions.

The company behind Temu and Chinese platform Pinduoduo on Thursday said net profit edged 0.7% higher from a year earlier to 29.54 billion yuan, equivalent to $4.43 billion. Revenue was little changed at 108.34 billion yuan.

Analysts had expected net profit of 24.81 billion yuan on revenue of 115.67 billion yuan, according to a FactSet consensus.

"We remain in a strategic investment phase, focused on strengthening supply-chain capabilities and supporting our merchants," said Jun Liu, vice president of finance.

PDD's American depositary receipts rose nearly 9% premarket, pointing to brightening investor sentiment. Appetite for the Nasdaq-listed company has waned as sentiment on tech companies weakened, leaving PDD's stock down by about one third this year.

Citi analysts pointed to Temu's shrinking user base, with Europe leading the decline as PDD faces tighter regulations in the bloc. Temu's global monthly active users fell 17.8% on iOS and 11.2% on Android in September, Citi said, citing third-party estimates.

Adding to its headwinds, the European Commission earlier this week said measures Temu put in place to tackle illegal products sold on its platform were insufficient, including what it called a "weak" content moderation system and ineffective sanctions. A PDD spokesperson said the company disagrees with the commission's view and will respond to the findings.

Meanwhile, back home, subdued consumer sentiment is weighing on Pinduoduo's performance. Total retail sales of consumer goods grew just 1.1% during the first nine months of 2026, official data showed. Sales for this year's Singles' Day--China's biggest online-shopping event of the year--rose 4.8% from last year, according to data provider Syntun.

data.title: Polymarket Indicates 29% Chance Anthropic's Market Cap Lands Above $1.5 Trillion — WSJ
data.description:
By Rebecca Feng

Bets on prediction-markets platform Polymarket give a 21% chance that Anthropic's market capitalization by the end of today will land between $1.5 trillion and $1.75 trillion, and 8% odds that it would land between $1.75 trillion and $2.75 trillion.

Put together, the bets imply a roughly 29% chance of a market debut that would see the stock pop 36%, and an almost 80% chance of shares rising 14% above the IPO price on the first day.

Anthropic's shares were priced at $83 apiece at the company's initial public offering, a level that would put the Claude maker's market cap at around $1.1 trillion based on a basic share count. This doesn't include so-called fully diluted shares which would include stock yet to be issued via options. (On that basis, the company's value at the IPO price is around $1.5 trillion.)

The Polymarket bet looks at Anthropic's market cap based on the basic share-count method. Anthropic's shares are trading 25% above its IPO price in the gray market, indicating a share price of $105 apiece, or a market cap of around $1.375 trillion.

Polymarket has a data partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of The Wall Street Journal.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Johnson Matthey says demand for pollution filters used at AI data centres outstrips supply
data.description:
Key points:
  • Cormetech acquisition closed in July
  • CEO Liam Condon says equipment additions are needed to expand output
  • Data centres are increasingly turning to wind turbines to ease pressure on power grids

By Nithyashree R B and Yadarisa Shabong

Demand for pollution filters used at AI data centres is far outstripping supply, Johnson Matthey CEO Liam Condon said on Thursday, as the company raised its annual sales expectations for its stationary emissions control businesses.

Data centres, whose construction is surging notably in the US as big tech companies pour money into AI computing and spurring demand for power, are increasingly turning to gas turbines to overcome grid constraints. That is also boosting demand for emission controls that need to be installed to meet regulations.

Britain's Johnson Matthey, which mainly makes pollution filters for cars and trucks, completed its acquisition in July of Cormetech, a US-based maker of catalysts that strip nitrogen oxides from gas-turbine exhaust.

"For some time, we've had to turn away potential customers because demand far outstrips supply at this stage of the market," Condon told Reuters after the company reported higher first-half operating profit.

Condon said on an analyst call that Johnson Matthey has the manufacturing capacity to boost production, but would need to buy more machines and dryers to make more products.

The market for selective catalytic reduction (SCR) systems — which reduce emissions — is worth about $1 billion and is expected to grow 10% to 15% annually over the next five to seven years mainly driven by data centres, Condon told Reuters in June after the company announced the Cormetech deal.

Other players in the SCR market include Belgium's Umicore , Austria's CERAM and parts of German ​chemicals group BASF .

Johnson Matthey raised its annual sales expectation for Cormetech and its Clean Air Solutions business, which serves the stationary emissions market in the marine, industrial and utilities sectors, to more than £250 million ($328 million), from more than £200 million previously.

The company will report the two businesses as its Clean Power segment from full year 2026/27.

($1 = 0.7614 pounds)

data.title: Siemens Energy signs 200-MW electrolyser deal for Swedish e-SAF site
data.description:
November 19 (Renewables Now) - Siemens Energy AG (ETR:ENR) has been tapped to supply around 200 MW of electrolysis capacity for Alby PtX’s planned sustainable aviation fuel (e-SAF) plant in Sweden, which is designed to produce 66,000 tonnes of e-SAF per year.

Selected as the electrolyser original equipment manufacturer (OEM), the German firm will initially deliver a basic engineering design package. Final equipment procurement remains subject to a positive final investment decision (FID) by Alby PtX.

The e-SAF project, planned in the municipality of Ange, will use renewable electricity to produce hydrogen using Siemens Energy's Elyzer P-300 proton exchange membrane (PEM) technology. The green hydrogen will then be combined with captured CO2 to make synthetic aviation fuel.

The agreement with Siemens Energy completes the project's core partner set-up, adding to a list already including Spanish engineering company Tecnicas Reunidas, which is leading the front-end engineering design (FEED), and technology partners Topsoe and Sasol.

The partners will work on refining the plant design, cost estimates and implementation schedule ahead of the FID.

data.title: BABA Stock Edges Lower Premarket After Q2 Earnings — Alibaba’s Adjusted Earnings Miss Estimates, AI Cloud Revenue Jumps 53%
data.description:
Key points:
  • The company reported revenue of RMB271.52 billion ($40.50 billion), roughly matching analyst estimates of $40.49 billion, according to Koyfin.
  • Alibaba E-commerce Group’s adjusted EBITA surged 243% to RMB38.85 billion, driven primarily by reduced losses in its China Quick Commerce business.
  • CFO Toby Xu said Alibaba will continue disciplined AI investments focused on returns while targeting positive free cash flow as AI monetization grows.

Alibaba Group (BABA) on Thursday reported September-quarter results, with revenue broadly in line with estimates as its AI Cloud and Compute Services business continued to gain momentum, posting 53% year-over-year growth.

However, the company reported non-GAAP diluted earnings of $1.21 per American depositary share (ADS), below analysts' estimate of $1.65, according to Koyfin. “Our full-stack AI capabilities continue to improve commercialization and delivered a strong quarter,” CEO Eddie Wu said. He added that recurring revenue from external Alibaba Cloud customers grew 67%, accelerating overall cloud revenue growth.

BABA shares were down 1.5% in premarket trading at the time of writing, after falling to a 22-month low on Wednesday, the lowest level seen since January 2025.

AI Cloud Growth Remains Strong, But Spending Weighs On Cash Flow

The company reported revenue of RMB271.52 billion ($40.50 billion), roughly matching analyst estimates of $40.49 billion, according to Koyfin data. Meanwhile, AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue reached RMB60.97 billion ($9.09 billion), up 53% year-over-year.

AI-related product revenue reached RMB17.92 billion ($2.67 billion), marking its 13th consecutive quarter of triple-digit year-over-year growth. Alibaba said demand for its AI and cloud services was broadening beyond AI labs, with customers across the internet, automotive, financial services and biotechnology sectors expanding their use of its services.

However, the expansion of its AI infrastructure continued to weigh on cash generation. Capital expenditure rose 60% year-over-year , as Alibaba increased investment in computing capacity to meet customer demand. Free cash flow was an outflow of RMB34.47 billion ($5.14 billion), compared with an outflow of RMB21.84 billion in the year-ago quarter. The company attributed the wider outflow mainly to higher cloud infrastructure expenditure.

Chief Financial Officer Toby Xu said Alibaba would continue investing in AI capabilities while focusing on returns. “As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow,” he said.

E-Commerce Profitability Improves

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, and amortization (EBITA) for Alibaba E-commerce Group rose 243% year over year to RMB38.85 billion. The company attributed the increase primarily to a significant reduction in losses at its China Quick Commerce business.

Taobao Instant Commerce continued to improve its unit economics quarter over quarter while maintaining market share, Alibaba said. However, customer management revenue, which includes marketing and commission-related revenue from merchants, declined 5%. Excluding the revenue impact of the company's new business development program, it would have increased 1% on a like-for-like basis.

How Retail Views BABA

Retail sentiment surrounding the stock on Stocktwits remained ‘extremely bullish’ over the past 24 hours, amid ‘extremely high’ message volumes. BABA was also one of the platform's trending tickers at the time of writing.

BABA shares have dropped over 42% year-to-date.

(Exchange Rate US$1 = RMB 6.705)

data.title: Swiss gold exports down 34% in October as UK deliveries fall
data.description:
Swiss gold exports fell to 109.7 metric tons in October, down 34% from the prior month as deliveries to Britain were lower, Swiss customs data showed on Thursday.

Exports from Switzerland, the world's biggest bullion refining and transit hub, to Britain slid to 38.4 tons in October from 126.2 tons in September. Britain is home to the world's largest over-the-counter gold trading market.

Shipments to China, a major gold consumer, jumped to 32.9 tons, their highest since March, from 12.7 tons in September, while exports to India rose to 10.8 tons from 3.1 tons, data showed.

Supporting demand from price-sensitive Indian buyers are lower gold prices , down 10% so far this quarter having hit their 14-month low of $3,693 per ounce on Thursday.

data.title: India rates hit 19-month peak; Thai prices highest in nearly two years
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indian rice export prices hit highest since April 2025
  • Concerns over weather support Indian, Thai prices
  • Vietnam prices fall to three-week low

By Vishak Mathew and Rajendra Jadhav

Indian rice export prices climbed to their highest in more than 19 months this week, buoyed by a stronger rupee and robust demand from Africa, while rates for the Thai variety rose to their highest level in nearly two years.

India's 5% broken parboiled variety (RI-INBKN5-P1) was quoted at $394-$398 per ton this week, up from last week’s $385-$390. Indian 5% broken white rice was priced at $395-$400 per ton.

"Higher domestic paddy prices, sustained African demand and rupee appreciation have played a vital role in supporting Indian rice export prices over the last three-four weeks," said Niraj Kumar, head of India rice business at Aditya Birla Global Trading.

"Concerns over below-normal monsoon rainfall and adverse weather conditions have further contributed to market firmness," he said.

Despite lower production, Indian rice exports are set to rise this year and next, the US Department of Agriculture forecasts, supported by ample stocks.

Thailand's 5% broken rice (RI-THBKN5-P1) rose to $505-$510 per ton this week, the highest since December 2024 and up from $495-$500 quoted last week.

One trader said additional purchases by regular buyers in the Philippines and Indonesia likely helped lift export prices, with sporadic buying from Japan. Another trader attributed the increase to higher domestic prices.

The same trader said market concerns that El Niño could reduce crop output have also contributed to keeping rice prices elevated.

Overall, Thai supplies remained steady in the near term, traders said, and the next crop was expected to reach the market early next year.

Vietnam's 5% broken rice (RI-VNBKN5-P1) was offered at $475-$485 per metric ton, down from $490-$495 a week ago.

"Prices fell due to the lack of buyers at higher prices," a trader based in Ho Chi Minh City said.

Vietnam exported 268,397 metric tons of rice in the first half of November, according to the government’s customs data. This raised the country's total rice shipments this year to November 15 to 7.18 million tons, valued at $3.48 billion.

Elsewhere, rice prices in Bangladesh remained elevated despite adequate domestic stocks, hitting consumers hard as they continued to grapple with stubbornly high inflation, traders said.

data.title: Norwegian Krone Faces Limited Downward Correction if Middle East Tensions Ease — Market Talk
data.description:
1225 GMT - The Norwegian krone could correct slightly lower once there are clear signs of a sustained easing in Middle East tensions that lead to lower energy prices, Commerzbank's Antje Praefcke says in a note. In this case, the euro could rise to as high as 11.00 kroner from 10.6472 kroner currently given Norway is a major oil and gas producer. "Nevertheless, revenues from oil and gas exports continue to pour in, meaning that even after such a correction, the krone should ultimately give up only limited ground." Gas prices are likely to remain high for some time and fall only slowly. Moreover, Norway benefits from solid public finances, the analyst adds. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

1218 GMT - The United Arab Emirates' economy is expected to grow 7.3% in 2027 after expanding just 0.2% this year, assuming regional disruptions ease, the International Monetary Fund says. The Middle East conflict affected hydrocarbon production and key nonoil sectors during the second quarter, although oil output has since recovered. Hydrocarbon growth is projected at 13.3% next year, compared with 2.3% in 2026, while nonoil activity is expected to grow 5.4% after contracting 0.5% this year. Inflation is forecast to ease to around 3% in 2027 from 5% this year. The IMF expects the country's fiscal surplus to narrow to near balance in 2026 before recovering next year, while its current-account surplus is also projected to shrink significantly amid disruptions to trade and travel. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

1211 GMT - Cryptocurrencies, including bitcoin, might benefit from the completion of Anthropic's initial public offering, XM analyst Achilleas Georgolopoulos says in a note. Investors who failed to secure Anthropic shares could return to cryptocurrencies, he says. The dollar's current pullback is also helping bitcoin pause its recent decline, he says. However, the dollar's continued strength, high real yields adjusted for inflation and expectations for further Federal Reserve interest-rate rises limit bitcoin's recovery, he says. Bitcoin rises 2.4% to $63,768, having reached a four-month low of $62,026 on Sunday, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

1201 GMT - The dollar is likely to remain higher for longer due to the positive implications of the AI boom, Deutsche Bank's George Saravelos says in a note. The AI boom has attracted massive equity inflows, boosted U.S. growth, prompted renewed U.S. inflation pressures and supported expectations for further interest-rate rises by the Federal Reserve, the analyst says. "We see some dollar strength into the first half of 2027, and then modest weakness in the second half of 2027 that would still leave the dollar very elevated." The DXY dollar index falls 0.2% to 103.658 as oil prices ease after reaching a 19-month high of 103.974 overnight. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

1159 GMT - Qatar's economy is expected to contract about 14.5% in 2026 as the Middle East war disrupts hydrocarbon production and exports, before rebounding from next year, the International Monetary Fund says. The contraction follows 1.8% growth in 2025, while nonoil activity grew about 3% in the first half of 2026. Growth is projected to average about 6% annually during 2028-31 as liquefied natural gas production normalizes and capacity expands. Inflation is expected to reach around 3.5% this year before easing toward 2% over the medium term. The IMF says fiscal revenue fell sharply in the first half due to lower hydrocarbon receipts, but expects the fiscal balance to return to surplus and the current-account surplus to reach double-digit levels over the medium term. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

1144 GMT - Corporate bonds issued by French companies look attractive as the businesses have well diversified cash flows and solid credit profiles, the UBS Global Wealth Management team says in a note. French credit spreads have widened in recent months due to concerns about the volatile political environment. Despite the bonds' underperformance, UBS has a largely positive outlook on French corporate bonds. However, selectivity and caution are necessary when choosing lower-rated French financial bonds and high-yield bonds, the team says. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

1002 GMT - The U.S. dollar holds near a 19-month high, while Treasury yields edge higher, as expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening continue to support both assets, says Kudo.com's Konstantinos Chrysikos in a note. "Markets still price in a 25-basis-point hike in December and several further increases through 2027," he says. Minutes of the Fed's October meeting also showed that policymakers mostly agreed that further hikes would be needed, he says. The DXY dollar index falls 0.2% to 103.699, having reached 103.974 overnight, its highest level since April 2025. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

1000 GMT - Sterling falls to a one-week low against the euro on reduced expectations for another interest-rate rise by the Bank of England in December. U.K. inflation data on Wednesday showed softer-than-expected services inflation for October. "Since this is roughly correlated with labor market data (such as the number of vacancies) it suggested that there was still little convincing evidence that second-order price effects are rising," Rabobank's Jane Foley says in a note. This argues against further rate increases, she says. The euro rises 0.2% to as high as 0.8365 pounds. Markets see a 75% chance of a December rate increase, down from 90% before this week's jobs and inflation data, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0956 GMT - Most investors who bought bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter are significantly underwater, according to Bitfinex Alpha. Over 90% of the inflows into bitcoin ETFs in 3Q arrived between Aug. 17 and Sept. 25 at an average entry price of around $80,070 during the period. Buyers in that window are down about 19%, Bitfinex says. The analysts say those clients mostly comprise wealth management clients of large banks and hedge funds. Bitcoin is up 2.5% at $63,836, but down over 25% year-to-date as a host of pressures weigh on the flagship cryptocurrency of late. (joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)

0943 GMT - The biggest risk to Spain's economy from a potential right-wing government is disruption to migration and a resultant squeeze on the labor force, economists at JPMorgan write in a note to clients. The country is set to hold elections next week, with surveys pointing to a coalition between the center-right People's Party and far-right Vox. The latter would likely look to crack down on irregular migration and block pathways to regularization, posing an obstacle to the labor boom that has helped Spain's economy outperform in recent years, JPM says. Still, there are constraints on how much a right-wing administration could do to reduce migration, the bank says, noting potential EU legal issues as well as recognition on the part of party leaders that migrants are key to the workforce in an era of demographic challenge. (joshua.kirby@wsj.com; @joshualeokirby)

0936 GMT - Markets narrowly cut their expectations of the Bank of England increasing interest rates at the December 17 meeting following this week's U.K. jobs and inflation data releases. The data indicated resilient activity but showed no evidence of high energy prices spreading into broader domestic inflation pressures, MUFG Bank's Henry Cook says in a note. MUFG expects the BOE could keep interest rates on hold in December and raise rates in February 2027. "The degree of urgency will be determined by developments in pay settlements, November CPI and energy pricing ahead of the next meeting." Markets expect a 75% chance of a BOE rate increase in December, down from 90% before the jobs and inflation data, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0904 GMT - The rising possibility of the U.S. Federal Reserve increasing interest rates in quick succession at upcoming policy meetings is keeping the dollar strong, MUFG's Lee Hardman says in a note. The minutes from the last Fed meeting released on Wednesday showed that nearly all members would likely vote to increase interest rates in the coming months, supporting market expectations of rate hikes. The DXY dollar index falls 0.1% to 103.735 after hitting a 19-month high of 103.974 overnight, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
